s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive skin lesions with systemic involvement
salient_findings: Purpura and ecchymoses with progression over 12 months
Abnormal liver function test results and renal impairment
key_facts: 1-year history of purpura, ecchymoses, anorexia, and weight loss
Medical history of alcohol abuse and cognitive impairment
Purpura and ecchymoses initially periorbital, progressed over 12 months
Elder abuse excluded
Waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura in multiple body regions
Anemia, abnormal liver function test results, and renal impairment with moderate proteinuria
Normal serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results
Unremarkable radiological studies
Punch biopsy showed upper dermal amorphous eosinophilic deposits
Congo red staining was positive
Polarizing light microscopy demonstrated pale apple-green birefringence

shortlist.label: Primary systemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Congo red staining was positive and polarizing light microscopy demonstrated pale apple-green birefringence, consistent with amyloid deposits

shortlist.label: Secondary systemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic inflammation or infection can cause secondary amyloidosis, and the patient has a history of alcohol abuse and cognitive impairment

shortlist.label: Amyloid light-chain amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms, such as purpura and ecchymoses, are consistent with amyloid light-chain amyloidosis, and the normal serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results do not rule out this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Lipoid proteinosis
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura are consistent with lipoid proteinosis, a rare condition characterized by the deposition of hyaline material in the skin and other tissues

shortlist.label: Primary amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms and biopsy results are consistent with primary amyloidosis, and this diagnosis should be considered in the differential diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura, particularly in the periorbital region, along with the biopsy findings of upper dermal amorphous eosinophilic deposits that are Congo red positive and demonstrate apple-green birefringence under polarized light, are characteristic of lipoid proteinosis.

rejected.label: Primary systemic amyloidosis
rejected.why: Normal SPEP and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results make this less likely

rejected.label: Secondary systemic amyloidosis
rejected.why: Clinical presentation and biopsy findings are more specific for lipoid proteinosis

rejected.label: Amyloid light-chain amyloidosis
rejected.why: Normal SPEP and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Primary amyloidosis
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes primary systemic amyloidosis, and the specific findings point more towards lipoid proteinosis
